events.title: Justinian I begins building the new Hagia Sophia
events.description: Only weeks after the second basilica was destroyed, Emperor Justinian I began the construction of a third, larger church, designed by Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus. The Hagia Sophia was completed in 537.

events.title: Wu Zetian abdicates and the Tang dynasty is restored
events.description: Wu Zetian, the only woman to rule China as emperor in her own right, gave up the throne, and her self-styled Zhou dynasty was abolished in favour of the restored Tang. She had ruled alone since 690.
events.html: Wu Zetian, the only woman to rule China as emperor in her own right, gave up the throne, and her self-styled Zhou dynasty was abolished in favour of the restored Tang. She had ruled alone since 690.

events.title: Traditional date for the completion of the Gutenberg Bible
events.description: By tradition, Johannes Gutenberg's Bible was completed in Mainz around this date. It was the first major book printed in Europe with movable metal type, and print spread rapidly across the continent.

events.title: George Frideric Handel is born in Halle
events.description: Handel trained in Germany and Italy before settling in London, where he wrote operas, the 'Water Music' and the oratorio 'Messiah'. He became a naturalised British subject in 1727.

events.title: Siege of the Alamo begins
events.description: Santa Anna's Mexican army surrounded the Texian garrison in the Alamo mission at San Antonio. After thirteen days the defenders, including Jim Bowie and Davy Crockett, were killed in the final assault.
events.html: Santa Anna's Mexican army surrounded the Texian garrison in the Alamo mission at San Antonio. After thirteen days the defenders, including Jim Bowie and Davy Crockett, were killed in the final assault.

events.title: Lincoln arrives secretly in Washington
events.description: Warned of a plot to kill him in Baltimore, President-elect Lincoln travelled through the city overnight in secret. He was mocked for the manner of his arrival, ten days before his inauguration.

events.title: Rotary Club founded in Chicago
events.description: Lawyer Paul Harris and three business acquaintances met to found the first Rotary Club. Rotary International now has some 1.4 million members and led the campaign to eradicate polio.

events.title: US Marines raise the flag on Mount Suribachi
events.description: Marines planted the US flag on the summit of Iwo Jima's volcano. Joe Rosenthal's photograph of the second, larger flag won the Pulitzer Prize, though the fighting went on for another month.
